AI.motivation: High-quality teleoperation datasets are expensive to collect, especially for hard tasks. Many tasks exhibit directional asymmetry where forward hard tasks are difficult, but reversing them by relaxing/disrupting the environment is comparatively easy. This asymmetry suggests reversed easy-task trajectories can serve as scalable supervision signals for hard tasks, reducing manual demonstration costs.
AI.method: Three key components: (1) Closed-loop data collection pipeline alternating between hard-task and easy-task policies to autonomously reset environment and generate diverse trajectories; (2) Hierarchical data refinement pipeline temporally inverting easy-task rollouts and filtering low-quality motion using kinematic priors and a critic-guided advantage filter; (3) Iterative policy learning training hard-task policy using both initial reversed easy-task demonstrations and filtered reversed data in continuous online learning loop.
AI.result: Across two simulated benchmarks and real-robot experiments, the method improves hard-task success rates with higher data efficiency and more stable training compared to reversal-based and reinforcement-learning baselines, without requiring extensive hard-task teleoperation.
AI.conclusion: By combining automated collection, hierarchical refinement, and iterative learning, the framework enables scalable, reliable training of complex, high-precision manipulation tasks with reduced manual teleoperation costs.

title: Joint On-and-Off Policy Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) necessitates an embodied agent to navigate in the physical world by adhering to natural language instructions. Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLM) have propelled the development of VLM-based VLN methods with two predominant paradigms: (1) imitation learning (IL) on expert demonstrations, followed by the Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) algorithm to bolster error recovery capabilities; (2) reinforcement learning (RL) driven by verifiable rewards to enhance reasoning and exploration. A notable gap is the absence of integration between these two distinct paradigms. This paper introduces JOP-VLN, a novel VLN framework that synergistically combines off-policy imitation learning and on-policy exploration within a three-stage training pipeline. Initially, IL is employed on expert demonstrations to acquire basic navigation skills. Subsequently, the DAgger algorithm is utilized to generate heuristic exploration trajectories, which are then used for imitation learning to improve error recovery capabilities. Finally, a joint on-and-off policy learning framework is implemented, featuring high-entropy trajectory sampling to enhance RL training efficiency and an error-correction-prioritized trajectory sorting strategy for effective error correction. Extensive experiments demonstrate the efficacy of JOP-VLN, achieving success rates of 69.9% and 68.0% on the VLN-CE R2R and RxR benchmarks, respectively, setting a new state-of-the-art on R2R. Project page: https://qingrongh.github.io/JOP-VLN.

AI.tldr: JOP-VLN is a novel VLN framework that synergistically combines off-policy imitation learning and on-policy exploration in a three-stage training pipeline, achieving state-of-the-art success rates of 69.9% (R2R) and 68.0% (RxR) on VLN benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) has two predominant paradigms - imitation learning with DAgger and reinforcement learning - but there is a notable gap in integrating these two distinct approaches for more effective navigation.
AI.method: A three-stage training pipeline: (1) IL on expert demonstrations for basic skills; (2) DAgger generates heuristic exploration trajectories for imitation learning to improve error recovery; (3) Joint on-and-off policy learning with high-entropy trajectory sampling and error-correction-prioritized trajectory sorting.
AI.result: Achieves 69.9% success rate on VLN-CE R2R and 68.0% on RxR benchmarks, setting a new state-of-the-art on R2R.
AI.conclusion: The synergistic combination of off-policy imitation learning and on-policy exploration effectively enhances error recovery capabilities and navigation performance in VLN tasks.

title: EgoHTR: Egocentric 4D Demonstrations of Human Terrain Traversal
summary: Deploying humanoid robots in unstructured terrain remains an open problem. While classic reinforcement learning struggles with the sheer complexity of real-world interactions, more promising methods leveraging human priors remain limited to models lacking contextual awareness. The restricted motion synthesis is a direct consequence of existing dataset pipelines failing to capture human-scene sequences in challenging environments. To bridge this gap between humanoid learning and scene reconstruction, we introduce the Egocentric Human-Terrain Reconstruction (EgoHTR) dataset. We develop and open-source a reconstruction pipeline capturing 55 scene-aligned 4D human motion sequences in diverse, complex environments using a multi-sensor setup of egocentric wearables and a portable 3D scanner. The resulting dataset comprises over 150k frames, which we evaluate against motion-capture ground truth, demonstrating state-of-the-art accuracy and establishing a rigorous benchmark for human motion analysis and synthesis. Further, we leverage this data to train perceptive locomotion policies, demonstrating hardware deployment on a Unitree G1 for reconstructed reference motions. Our pipeline enables community-driven dataset extensions and factors the problem to help researchers build foundational, context-aware robots that reliably traverse uneven terrain.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Egocentric Human-Terrain Reconstruction (EgoHTR) dataset, a comprehensive collection of 55 scene-aligned 4D human motion sequences in complex environments, enabling context-aware humanoid robot deployment in unstructured terrain.
AI.motivation: Deploying humanoid robots in unstructured terrain is challenging due to: 1) Classic reinforcement learning struggles with real-world interaction complexity, 2) Human-prior-based methods lack contextual awareness, 3) Existing datasets fail to capture human-scene sequences in challenging environments, limiting motion synthesis capabilities.
AI.method: Developed and open-sourced a reconstruction pipeline using multi-sensor setup of egocentric wearables and a portable 3D scanner, capturing 55 scene-aligned 4D human motion sequences in diverse, complex environments, resulting in a dataset of over 150k frames.
AI.result: Demonstrated state-of-the-art accuracy against motion-capture ground truth. Successfully trained perceptive locomotion policies using this data and achieved hardware deployment on a Unitree G1 robot for reconstructed reference motions.
AI.conclusion: The pipeline enables community-driven dataset extensions and factors the problem to help researchers build foundational, context-aware robots that reliably traverse uneven terrain, bridging the gap between humanoid learning and scene reconstruction.

title: Deformable State Estimation for Autonomous Surgical Tissue Retraction Under Partial Observability
comment: Accepted to the ICRA 2026 RASEI Workshop
summary: Surgical tissue retraction requires effective manipulation planning under partial and noisy perception. We study state estimation for deformable tissue retraction, where only sparse observations of the tissue surface are available at decision time. We propose a learned state estimator that reconstructs the full deformable mesh state from 40 noisy vertex observations. The estimator combines a multilayer perceptron with a low-dimensional PCA latent representation and is trained using geometry-aware regularization that encourages smooth and physically plausible deformations. We evaluate the approach in a 2D deformable sheet simulation using single-step and multi-step retraction planning. Results show that the learned estimator achieves 98.1% of oracle performance in multi-step retraction while supporting efficient inference. These results demonstrate that learned, geometry-regularized state estimation can support effective deformable manipulation under realistic perception constraints.

AI.tldr: A learned state estimator for deformable tissue retraction that reconstructs full deformable mesh states from sparse, noisy observations using geometry-aware regularization, achieving near-oracle performance.
AI.motivation: Surgical tissue retraction requires effective manipulation planning under partial and noisy perception constraints where only sparse observations are available at decision time.
AI.method: A learned state estimator that reconstructs full deformable mesh state from 40 noisy vertex observations, combining a multilayer perceptron with low-dimensional PCA latent representation, trained using geometry-aware regularization that encourages smooth and physically plausible deformations.
AI.result: The learned estimator achieves 98.1% of oracle performance in multi-step retraction while supporting efficient inference.
AI.conclusion: Learned, geometry-regularized state estimation can support effective deformable manipulation under realistic perception constraints.

title: VAMP-MR: Vector-Accelerated Motion Planning and Execution for Multi-Robot-Arms
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. To appear in the Proceedings of IROS 2026
summary: Multi-robot-arm motion planning is a key challenge in deploying multiple manipulators for industrial tasks such as manufacturing. Existing search-based and sampling-based solvers often require significant computation time to produce collision-free, high-quality motions suitable for safe real-world execution. In this work, we introduce a new suite of multi-robot-arm motion planners capable of near real-time motion generation, combining classical planning algorithms with state-of-the-art vectorized collision-checking techniques. Based on CPU SIMD instructions, our new planners accelerate their primary bottleneck, collision checking, and achieve up to two orders of magnitude speedup in both motion planning and execution postprocessing for multi-arm manipulation tasks. We also release our implementation to lower the barrier for research and development of multi-robot-arm planning and manipulation problems. Code is available at https://vamp-mr.github.io/vamp-mr

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new suite of multi-robot-arm motion planners combining classical planning algorithms with CPU SIMD-based vectorized collision-checking techniques, achieving up to two orders of magnitude speedup in motion planning and execution postprocessing for multi-arm manipulation tasks.
AI.motivation: Multi-robot-arm motion planning is a key challenge in deploying multiple manipulators for industrial tasks such as manufacturing. Existing search-based and sampling-based solvers often require significant computation time to produce collision-free, high-quality motions suitable for safe real-world execution.
AI.method: The researchers combine classical planning algorithms with state-of-the-art vectorized collision-checking techniques based on CPU SIMD instructions, accelerating the primary bottleneck of collision checking.
AI.result: The new planners achieve up to two orders of magnitude speedup in both motion planning and execution postprocessing for multi-arm manipulation tasks.
AI.conclusion: The implementation is released to lower the barrier for research and development of multi-robot-arm planning and manipulation problems. Code is available at https://vamp-mr.github.io/vamp-mr.

title: Topology-Agnostic Mesh Reconstruction of Deformable Objects from Sparse Touch
comment: Accepted to the RSS 2026 DAROMA Workshop
summary: Estimating the full shape of a deformable object is especially challenging when vision is unavailable: in the dark, inside an opaque bag, behind the manipulating hand, or under heavy self-occlusion. Touch is the natural sensor in these settings, but touches are sparse and local. We present a single topology-agnostic estimator that reconstructs the full mesh of a deformable object from only a few touches and no vision, using one permutation-invariant cross-attention architecture that handles a 1D rope, a 2D cloth, and a 3D volumetric soft body. The learned estimator reduces reconstruction error by roughly two-thirds relative to non-learned geometric mesh completion and a Gaussian-process surface baseline, and it outperforms a simpler global-pool set encoder, with the gap growing as more touches are observed. We then show that the estimator's deep-ensemble uncertainty can be used to learn where to touch next, which lowers error further and beats both random touching and a Gaussian-process active baseline at sparse budgets. This gain is modest on average but grows with self-occlusion and on the error tail. When vision is also available, where to touch barely matters, motivating the vision-free setting we study.

AI.tldr: A single topology-agnostic deep learning model reconstructs full mesh of deformable objects (rope, cloth, soft body) from sparse touch data without vision, using permutation-invariant cross-attention. The model reduces reconstruction error by ~67% vs baselines, and its uncertainty guides active touch sampling to further improve results.
AI.motivation: Estimating full shape of deformable objects is challenging when vision is unavailable (dark, opaque bag, behind hand, heavy self-occlusion). Touch is natural but sparse and local. Existing methods lack a unified approach across different object types.
AI.method: Permutation-invariant cross-attention architecture that handles 1D rope, 2D cloth, and 3D volumetric soft body. Uses deep-ensemble for uncertainty estimation to guide active touch sampling.
AI.result: Reduces reconstruction error by ~67% vs non-learned geometric mesh completion and Gaussian-process surface baseline. Outperforms simpler global-pool set encoder. Deep-ensemble uncertainty beats random touching and GP active baseline. Small gain on average but grows with self-occlusion and error tail.
AI.conclusion: The unified estimator works well for vision-free settings. When vision is available, touch location matters less, motivating the studied vision-free setting. The approach successfully bridges sparse local touch data with full object reconstruction across different topologies.

title: Layered Risk Mapping for Autonomous Patient Transport in Expeditionary Medical Facilities
summary: In expeditionary medical facilities, routine patient transport imposes a compounding burden of personal protective equipment consumption, staff diversion, and elevated infection risk that becomes unsustainable under surge conditions. While autonomous wheelchairs could absorb this operational load, the safety-critical nature of patient transit within these highly unstructured and dynamic environments poses complex navigational challenges. To address this, we present a layered risk mapping framework that fuses four heterogeneous environmental hazards (terrain slope, static and dynamic obstacles, and semantic traversability) into a unified probabilistic cost surface via a Noisy-OR fusion model. In a paired Monte-Carlo evaluation, risk-informed fusion reduces collision rates from over 73% to under 32% and more than doubles obstacle clearance relative to a risk-unaware baseline. Additionaly, Noisy-OR achieves the highest clearance to obstacles and the lowest conditional peak risk across all tested hazard densities. We further validate the framework on a commercial powered wheelchair across three representative mission profiles in indoor and outdoor deployments, demonstrating that this architecture successfully meets the planning requirements of this previously unaddressed operational regime.

AI.tldr: A layered risk mapping framework fuses terrain slope, static/dynamic obstacles, and semantic traversability into a unified probabilistic cost surface via Noisy-OR fusion, reducing collision rates from 73% to 32% and doubling obstacle clearance in autonomous wheelchair navigation for medical facilities.
AI.motivation: In expeditionary medical facilities, routine patient transport creates a compounding burden of personal protective equipment consumption, staff diversion, and elevated infection risk that becomes unsustainable under surge conditions. Autonomous wheelchairs could absorb this operational load, but the safety-critical nature of patient transit in unstructured, dynamic environments poses complex navigational challenges.
AI.method: A layered risk mapping framework that fuses four heterogeneous environmental hazards (terrain slope, static obstacles, dynamic obstacles, and semantic traversability) into a unified probabilistic cost surface using a Noisy-OR fusion model. The approach includes paired Monte-Carlo evaluations and validation on a commercial powered wheelchair across three mission profiles in indoor and outdoor deployments.
AI.result: Risk-informed fusion reduces collision rates from over 73% to under 32% and more than doubles obstacle clearance relative to a risk-unaware baseline. Noisy-OR achieves the highest obstacle clearance and lowest conditional peak risk across all tested hazard densities.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully meets the planning requirements of autonomous wheelchair navigation in expeditionary medical facilities, demonstrating viability for this previously unaddressed operational regime.

title: Improving Map Consistency in Graph-Based LiDAR SLAM Through Information-Aware Odometry and Retroactive Loop Closure
summary: High-quality maps are fundamental for robotics tasks such as navigation and planning. Although modern graph-based LiDAR SLAM systems achieve good trajectory accuracies, a low trajectory error alone does not guarantee geometrically consistent maps, particularly at revisit locations where missed loop closures and residual drift can produce local misalignments. In this work, we address the problem of jointly improving global trajectory estimation and local map quality in 3D LiDAR SLAM. We first propose a framework to efficiently estimate geometry-dependent information matrices for ICP, enabling principled weighting of odometry constraints in a pose graph. We then introduce a hierarchical loop-closure module that decouples place recognition from geometric registration, together with a retroactive loop-closure module that exploits the optimized pose graph to recover missed loop closures. We also propose an evaluation protocol to measure map consistency at revisit locations. We evaluate our SLAM system on several datasets against state-of-the-art LiDAR SLAM systems. Experimental results demonstrate global trajectory accuracies on par with or better than existing methods while consistently improving local geometric map consistency at revisit locations. These results suggest that coupling uncertainty-aware odometry with geometry-guided loop-closure refinement leads to more accurate trajectories and higher-quality maps.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a framework for improving both global trajectory estimation and local map quality in 3D LiDAR SLAM through geometry-dependent information matrices for ICP, hierarchical and retroactive loop-closure modules, and an evaluation protocol for measuring map consistency at revisit locations.
AI.motivation: While modern graph-based LiDAR SLAM systems achieve good trajectory accuracies, low trajectory error alone does not guarantee geometrically consistent maps, especially at revisit locations where missed loop closures and residual drift produce local misalignments.
AI.method: The proposed method includes: (1) a framework for efficiently estimating geometry-dependent information matrices for ICP to enable principled weighting of odometry constraints in pose graphs, (2) a hierarchical loop-closure module that decouples place recognition from geometric registration, (3) a retroactive loop-closure module that exploits the optimized pose graph to recover missed loop closures, and (4) an evaluation protocol to measure map consistency at revisit locations.
AI.result: Experimental results on several datasets demonstrate that the proposed system achieves global trajectory accuracies on par with or better than state-of-the-art LiDAR SLAM systems while consistently improving local geometric map consistency at revisit locations.
AI.conclusion: Coupling uncertainty-aware odometry with geometry-guided loop-closure refinement leads to more accurate trajectories and higher-quality maps in 3D LiDAR SLAM.

title: Kepler-Encoder-v0.1: Towards a Multimodal Embedding Model for Robots
summary: A robot must understand the state of its own body, but a camera sees only part of it. Force and contact leave almost no trace in a single frame, and raw vision features read force at $R^2$ at or below $0.10$ on every robot we test. We present Kepler-Encoder-v0.1, a robot-first multimodal encoder that treats robot state as a modality and fuses vision, proprioception, and force/torque into a single shared latent with a learned-query cross-attention layer, trained self-supervised by masked cross-modal prediction under the LeJEPA/SIGReg objective. At evaluation only vision enters, which poses a sharp question. Does fusing state into training make the vision-only latent carry anything the pixels do not already contain? On the RH20T corpus the answer is yes, precisely where the camera is weakest. On held-out scenes, the vision-only latent recovers end-effector state, and force in particular, significantly above both raw frozen-ViT features and a compute-matched vision-only control on every sensored robot, though absolute force recovery at a single timestep is modest; on motor state, which the camera largely sees, it is statistically tied with the strongest vision baselines, and it is the only feature whose latent geometry tracks state. A single embodiment-agnostic encoder covers four robots, and a data-matched control shows this breadth reflects embodiment diversity rather than data volume. The frozen latent is directly useful. Its own cross-modal prediction error is a training-free invalid-state monitor (AUROC $0.90$ on out-of-range states, $0.69$ on scene-swapped states), and a diffusion decoder (PixNerd) reconstructs the camera frame from the latent, confirming the spatial compression preserves world-state. This report validates the single-timestep case; native-rate temporal fusion is the next step.

AI.tldr: Kepler-Encoder-v0.1 is a robot-first multimodal encoder that fuses vision, proprioception, and force/torque into a shared latent space using a learned-query cross-attention layer, trained self-supervised under the LeJEPA/SIGReg objective. The vision-only latent recovers end-effector state and force significantly better than raw frozen ViT features, while matching vision-only baselines on motor state. The single-embodiment-agnostic encoder demonstrates that performance gains stem from embodiment diversity rather than data volume.
AI.motivation: A robot must understand its own body state, but cameras only see part of it and raw vision features read force at or below 0.10 R² across tested robots. The authors question whether fusing robot state (proprioception and force/torque) into training can make vision-only latents carry information beyond pixels, particularly where cameras are weakest.
AI.method: Kepler-Encoder-v0.1 uses a robot-first multimodal encoder that treats robot state as a modality, fusing vision, proprioception, and force/torque into a single shared latent via a learned-query cross-attention layer. Training is self-supervised using masked cross-modal prediction under the LeJEPA/SIGReg objective. The encoder is embodiment-agnostic and trained on four robots.
AI.result: On the RH20T corpus, the vision-only latent recovers end-effector state and force significantly above raw frozen ViT features and compute-matched vision-only baselines on every sensored robot. Absolute force recovery at a single timestep is modest. On motor state (which the camera largely sees), performance is statistically tied with the strongest vision baselines, and the latent geometry uniquely tracks state. The frozen latent's cross-modal prediction error serves as a training-free invalid-state monitor (AUROC 0.90 on out-of-range states, 0.69 on scene-swapped states), and a diffusion decoder (PixNerd) reconstructs camera frames from the latent, confirming spatial compression preserves world-state.
AI.conclusion: The research validates that fusing robot state into training creates vision-only latents that contain information beyond pixels, precisely where cameras are weakest. A single embodiment-agnostic encoder covers four robots, and performance gains reflect embodiment diversity rather than data volume. The frozen latent is directly useful for invalid-state monitoring and world-state reconstruction, establishing that single-timestep fusion is effective—suggesting native-rate temporal fusion as the next step.

title: COLMAR: Cooperative View Policy Learning for Multi-Agent Active 3D Reconstruction
summary: Active 3D reconstruction requires selecting informative viewpoints under limited sensing budgets. In multi-agent settings, coordination inefficiencies such as redundant observations and spatial clustering can significantly reduce reconstruction quality. We present COLMAR, a cooperative view policy learning framework for multi-agent active 3D reconstruction. COLMAR formulates viewpoint allocation as a shared policy optimization over map-centric observations and introduces a reconstruction-aware objective that promotes overlap-aware coverage, team-level discovery, and collision-safe exploration. Dense feedback derived from incremental reconstruction updates aligns exploration behavior with downstream geometric quality. The policy is trained using parameter-sharing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with independent per-agent action selection at deployment, conditioned on a fused team map and without inter-agent message passing for decision making. Selected viewpoints are then reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for high-fidelity photometric evaluation. Experiments on GLEAM and Replica demonstrate consistent improvements over heuristic and non-cooperative baselines, achieving up to 54% higher reconstruction accuracy and 49% greater coverage under matched sensing budgets.

AI.tldr: COLMAR is a cooperative multi-agent active 3D reconstruction framework that uses shared policy optimization with reconstruction-aware objectives to coordinate viewpoint selection, achieving up to 54% higher reconstruction accuracy and 49% greater coverage than baselines.
AI.motivation: Active 3D reconstruction requires selecting informative viewpoints under limited sensing budgets. In multi-agent settings, coordination inefficiencies such as redundant observations and spatial clustering significantly reduce reconstruction quality.
AI.method: COLMAR formulates viewpoint allocation as a shared policy optimization over map-centric observations, introducing a reconstruction-aware objective that promotes overlap-aware coverage, team-level discovery, and collision-safe exploration. The policy is trained using parameter-sharing PPO with independent per-agent action selection, conditioned on a fused team map without inter-agent message passing. Selected viewpoints are reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting for evaluation.
AI.result: Experiments on GLEAM and Replica datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over heuristic and non-cooperative baselines, achieving up to 54% higher reconstruction accuracy and 49% greater coverage under matched sensing budgets.
AI.conclusion: COLMAR effectively addresses coordination inefficiencies in multi-agent active 3D reconstruction through its policy-based approach with reconstruction-aware objectives, achieving substantial improvements in both accuracy and coverage compared to existing methods.

title: Flow-aware Optimal Navigation in Unsteady Flows through Reinforcement Learning
summary: Autonomous robotic navigation in nonstationary time-varying fluid flows remains a fundamental challenge due to partial observability and the unpredictability of realistic environments. While classical optimal control frameworks employed in robotics require unrealistic a-priori global flow knowledge, biological systems are able to navigate successfully by exploiting localized sensory cues. In this work we present a reinforcement learning approach using the TD3 algorithm to train autonomous agents to reach arbitrary targets within a parametric, chaotic double-gyre flow. To investigate optimal sensory mechanisms, we evaluate five bio-inspired observation strategies based on relative position, local velocity or local vorticity measures, and short-term memory variants. Additionally, we analyze the impact of providing agents with explicit global flow parameters. Numerical results demonstrate that an agent that is able to sense and remember a set number of flow velocity measures achieves the highest performance. The experiments reveal a trade-off in sensor utility: velocity-aware agents optimize energy efficiency, whereas vorticity sensors provide superior structural mapping and achieve better target proximity. Incorporating explicit global flow parameters is shown to decrease navigation performance. This behavior suggests that reinforcement learning-based autonomous systems develop more robust and general policies when restricted to implicit flow representations. The presented results offer insights for improving the transition of bio-inspired robotic navigation from simulation to real-world environments.

AI.tldr: A TD3 reinforcement learning approach trains autonomous agents to navigate chaotic double-gyre flows using bio-inspired observation strategies (relative position, velocity, vorticity, short-term memory). Velocity-memory agents achieve highest performance, with velocity sensors optimizing energy efficiency and vorticity sensors providing superior structural mapping. Explicit global flow parameters actually reduce performance, suggesting implicit representations yield more robust policies.
AI.motivation: Classical optimal control frameworks require unrealistic a-priori global flow knowledge, whereas biological systems successfully navigate by exploiting localized sensory cues in nonstationary time-varying fluid flows.
AI.method: TD3 reinforcement learning algorithm trains agents in parametric chaotic double-gyre flow. Five bio-inspired observation strategies are evaluated: relative position, local velocity, local vorticity, and short-term memory variants. The impact of providing explicit global flow parameters is also analyzed.
AI.result: Agents capable of sensing and remembering flow velocity measures achieve highest performance. A trade-off exists: velocity-aware agents optimize energy efficiency, while vorticity sensors provide superior structural mapping and target proximity. Explicit global flow parameters decrease navigation performance.
AI.conclusion: Reinforcement learning-based autonomous systems develop more robust and general policies when restricted to implicit flow representations rather than explicit global parameters. These findings offer insights for transitioning bio-inspired robotic navigation from simulation to real-world environments.

title: IMMNet: Hybrid Fusion of Model-based and Data-driven Approaches for Maneuvering Target Tracking
summary: Maneuvering target tracking in three-dimensional space remains a challenging problem due to complex motion dynamics and model mismatch. To address this, this paper proposes a hybrid model/data-driven algorithm named IMMNet, which integrates the interpretable structure of the interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm with learnable neural components. Unlike end-to-end black-box methods, the proposed IMMNet algorithm not only can preserve the Bayesian inference mechanism that is essential for real-time radar applications, but also can adaptively learn motion patterns and noise characteristics from data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed IMMNet algorithm consistently outperforms the existing algorithms across various scenarios, validating it as a robust, interpretable, and practical solution for maneuvering target tracking.

AI.tldr: A hybrid IMM-neural network algorithm (IMMNet) that combines the interpretable structure of the interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm with learnable neural components for improved maneuvering target tracking in 3D space.
AI.motivation: Maneuvering target tracking in three-dimensional space remains challenging due to complex motion dynamics and model mismatch. Existing methods struggle to balance model interpretability with data-driven adaptability.
AI.method: IMMNet integrates the interpretable structure of the interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm with learnable neural components. Unlike end-to-end black-box methods, it preserves the Bayesian inference mechanism while enabling adaptive learning of motion patterns and noise characteristics from data.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that IMMNet consistently outperforms existing algorithms across various scenarios, showing superior tracking performance.
AI.conclusion: IMMNet is validated as a robust, interpretable, and practical solution for maneuvering target tracking applications.

title: Agile perceptive multi-skill locomotion for quadrupedal robots in the wild
comment: Project page: https://skillquadsr.github.io/ ,This is the author's version of the work. It is posted here by permission of the AAAS for personal use, not for redistribution. The definitive version was published in Science Robotics on 7.15.2026; doi: 10.1126/scirobotics.adz7397. Jun-Gill Kang and Jaehyun Park are co-first authors. Seungwoo Hong and Hae-Won Park are co-corresponding authors
summary: Enabling quadrupedal robots to traverse complex terrains-from rugged outdoor environments to urban landscapes-requires seamless integration of multiple motor skills, smooth transitions between gaits, and high-speed perceptive locomotion using only onboard sensors. We present APT-RL (Action Pretrained Transformer-based Reinforcement Learning), a unified framework that enables multi-skill locomotion to achieve high-speed traversal in complex environments through autonomous skill transitions utilizing only onboard perception and computation. Our approach generates large-scale, feature-rich 2D motion datasets through trajectory optimization with simplified dynamics. These datasets enable training of diverse, reusable locomotion skills that transfer effectively to a real quadruped robot operating on complex uneven terrains. The resulting high-quality skills serve as strong priors for efficient learning of complex downstream tasks and extend naturally to 3D environments, enabling smooth, high-speed multi-skill locomotion in deployed policy. Real-world experiments demonstrate the framework's capabilities: the robot performs agile maneuvers through complex indoor obstacles and outdoor wild environments, including dynamic drop-down maneuvers that reach instantaneous peak speeds of up to 6 meters per second. A single onboard policy enables robust traversal of diverse obstacles, including stairs, hurdles, stepping stones, gaps, and fallen branches, demonstrating the versatility and effectiveness of our approach.

AI.tldr: APT-RL is a unified framework that uses pretrained transformers and reinforcement learning to enable quadrupedal robots to achieve high-speed multi-skill locomotion in complex terrains using only onboard sensors.
AI.motivation: Quadrupedal robots need to traverse complex terrains (from rugged outdoor environments to urban landscapes) requiring seamless integration of multiple motor skills, smooth gait transitions, and high-speed perceptive locomotion using only onboard sensors.
AI.method: The framework generates large-scale, feature-rich 2D motion datasets through trajectory optimization with simplified dynamics. These datasets train diverse, reusable locomotion skills that serve as strong priors for efficient learning of complex downstream tasks and extend to 3D environments. Skills are trained via pretrained transformers combined with reinforcement learning.
AI.result: The robot performs agile maneuvers in complex indoor and outdoor environments, including dynamic drop-down maneuvers reaching instantaneous peak speeds of 6 m/s. A single onboard policy enables robust traversal of diverse obstacles including stairs, hurdles, stepping stones, gaps, and fallen branches.
AI.conclusion: APT-RL demonstrates that a unified framework with pretrained motion priors can enable robust, high-speed multi-skill locomotion in deployed policies using only onboard perception, achieving exceptional versatility and effectiveness across diverse terrains.

title: Active Trust Management for Successful Human-Robot Teaming: Moving from a Trust Repair to a Trust Satisficing Perspective
summary: Integrating mobile robots into human teams promises significant capability improvements for tasks such as searching hazardous environments. Unlike existing teleoperated robots, future robot systems will increasingly be endowed with some level of artificial intelligence (AI), giving them a degree of autonomy in how they pursue mission goals. This autonomy could make a human-agent (robot) team more effective but also put inter-agent trust under strain if robots make a mistake, or (appear to) pursue task priorities that conflict with the team's best interest. During a mission, agents' trust states are anticipated to vary according to the situation as understood by each teammate (trustor). If component-level (agent) or system-level trust falls below sufficient levels for cooperative tasks to be completed, it could critically affect mission success . We argue that active trust management will be an important precondition for the success of human-robot teams (HRTs, a subcategory of human-agent teams with embodied agents), especially in dynamic, high-risk environments. We present a trust satisficing perspective which acknowledges and attempts to account for the fluctuating, multi-faceted, and context-dependent nature of trust and trust requirements even under normal operating conditions. Our outline of a trust management framework for human-robot teaming includes online measurement of proxy metrics for trust, closed-loop adaptation of robot behavior, and variable autonomy to give space for human responsibility in situations requiring value judgements. We refer to a recent experimental exploration of 'swift trust' and a novel behavioral trust metric for HRT, and we highlight issues for further investigation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a trust management framework for human-robot teams (HRTs) that employs online trust measurement, closed-loop robot behavior adaptation, and variable autonomy to ensure trust levels remain sufficient for mission success in dynamic, high-risk environments.
AI.motivation: Mobile robots with AI autonomy can improve team capabilities in hazardous environments, but this autonomy may strain inter-agent trust if robots make mistakes or pursue conflicting task priorities. Active trust management is essential for HRT success, especially in dynamic, high-risk settings where trust states fluctuate based on each teammate's situational understanding.
AI.method: The authors present a trust satisficing perspective that acknowledges the fluctuating, multi-faceted, and context-dependent nature of trust. The proposed framework includes: 1) online measurement of proxy metrics for trust, 2) closed-loop adaptation of robot behavior, and 3) variable autonomy to allow human responsibility in situations requiring value judgments.
AI.result: The paper references a recent experimental exploration of "swift trust" and introduces a novel behavioral trust metric for HRTs.
AI.conclusion: Active trust management is identified as a critical precondition for successful human-robot teaming. The authors highlight several issues for further investigation to advance trust management in dynamic, high-risk environments.

title: Semantic Anchoring for Robotic Action Representations
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich semantic representations from pretrained Vision-Language Models, yet fine-tuning on limited robot demonstrations degrades this structure and undermines generalization. A fundamental question therefore arises: what constitutes a good action representation? Inspired by the mirror neuron theory's insight that observation and execution share an intention-level encoding, we examine whether a robot's action representations preserve the semantic structure captured by pretrained encoders. Systematic probing confirms that this structure erodes during finetuning, and that its quality synchronizes with both task success and out-of-distribution generalization. We further introduce a plug-and-play method that anchors action representations to a semantic manifold while decomposing representations into a shared semantic channel and a private channel, all discarded at inference, leaving the deployed model unchanged. Validated on different VLA backbones across simulation and real-world benchmarks, our method yields up to +18.7% on real-world in-distribution tasks and +21.5% on out-of-distribution generalization.

AI.tldr: A plug-and-play method that preserves semantic structure in VLA models during fine-tuning by anchoring representations to a semantic manifold, decomposing them into shared and private channels, improving in-distribution performance (+18.7%) and out-of-distribution generalization (+21.5%).
AI.motivation: VLA models inherit rich semantic representations from pretrained Vision-Language Models, but fine-tuning on limited robot demonstrations degrades this structure and undermines generalization. The fundamental question is what constitutes a good action representation.
AI.method: Inspired by mirror neuron theory, the method anchors action representations to a semantic manifold and decomposes them into a shared semantic channel (preserved) and a private channel (discarded at inference). This is a plug-and-play approach that leaves the deployed model unchanged.
AI.result: Systematic probing confirms semantic structure erodes during fine-tuning, and its quality synchronizes with task success and out-of-distribution generalization. The method yields +18.7% on real-world in-distribution tasks and +21.5% on out-of-distribution generalization across different VLA backbones in both simulation and real-world benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Preserving semantic structure during fine-tuning is crucial for both task success and generalization. The proposed method successfully maintains this structure through semantic manifold anchoring and channel decomposition, demonstrating significant improvements across diverse benchmarks.

title: An Empirical Study on Stage-Information Interfaces for VLA Fine-Tuning
summary: One high-level instruction in long-horizon manipulation can cover several action stages. We use segmented action annotations as an intermediate representation between the full-task instruction and VLA action chunks. A progress module tracks the active stage, while the action policy receives stage information either as current-stage text or as a normalized ordinal stage index in robot state. We compare these interfaces with GR00T N1.6 on LIBERO-10 under direct fine-tuning and continuation fine-tuning from a full-task instruction baseline. Under direct fine-tuning, full-task instruction, current-stage text, and Ordinal Stage-State achieve mean success rates of 57.45%, 50.24%, and 54.36%, respectively, showing that explicit stage information does not automatically improve the policy. Under continuation, the corresponding means are 49.07%, 50.00%, and 53.75%, with Ordinal Stage-State exceeding both alternatives in all three paired runs. The observed benefit differs across interface representations and training arrangements.

AI.tldr: This paper explores using segmented action annotations and different interface representations (full-task instruction, current-stage text, and Ordinal Stage-State) to improve long-horizon manipulation policies, finding that Ordinal Stage-State outperforms other interfaces under continuation fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require handling multiple action stages, and providing explicit stage information through different interfaces could potentially improve policy performance beyond just using full-task instructions.
AI.method: A progress module tracks active stages while comparing three interface representations for providing stage information to the action policy: 1) full-task instruction, 2) current-stage text, and 3) Ordinal Stage-State (normalized ordinal stage index in robot state). Experiments conducted on LIBERO-10 under direct fine-tuning and continuation fine-tuning from a full-task instruction baseline.
AI.result: Under direct fine-tuning: full-task instruction (57.45%), current-stage text (50.24%), Ordinal Stage-State (54.36%). Under continuation fine-tuning: full-task instruction (49.07%), current-stage text (50.00%), Ordinal Stage-State (53.75%). Ordinal Stage-State exceeds both alternatives in all three paired runs under continuation fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Explicit stage information does not automatically improve policy performance under direct fine-tuning, but Ordinal Stage-State provides consistent benefits under continuation fine-tuning, suggesting the benefit depends on both interface representation and training arrangement.

title: Design, Modeling and Experimental Validation of a Miniature Hybrid Underwater Glider With Large-Range Foldable Deflectable Wings
summary: Miniature hybrid underwater gliders have attracted increasing attention for long-endurance ocean observation and confined-space inspection. Large-range wing reconfiguration offers a promising yet largely unexplored approach for simultaneously enhancing maneuverability and shape adaptability in constrained underwater environments. However, such morphing introduces substantial challenges in mechanical integration, dynamic modeling, and hydrodynamic characterization. This paper presents FoDeGlider, a miniature hybrid underwater glider equipped with two independently actuated wings capable of large-range folding and deflection. To capture configuration-dependent variations in mass distribution, center-of-geometry location, and hydrodynamic loading, a multibody dynamics model is developed by treating wing configuration as a structural variable. A composite rigid body algorithm (CRBA)-based projection formulates the composite inertia, wrench transformations, and component-level hydrodynamics into a unified Fossen-form dynamic model applicable to arbitrary wing configurations. A sequential parameter-identification framework is further proposed to estimate fuselage and wing hydrodynamic coefficients, resulting in an open benchmark dataset for model identification and validation. Extensive experiments are conducted, the results of which demonstrate accurate dynamic modeling and parameter identification across diverse morphing configurations. Gate traversal experiments further validate FoDeGlider's ability to actively reconfigure its morphology during locomotion, enabling enhanced navigation in confined underwater environments.

AI.tldr: FoDeGlider is a miniature hybrid underwater glider with independently actuated wings that can fold and deflect over large ranges. The paper presents a multibody dynamics model using CRBA-based projection and a parameter identification framework to enable accurate dynamic modeling and active morphing for enhanced maneuverability in confined underwater environments.
AI.motivation: Large-range wing reconfiguration offers a promising approach for simultaneously enhancing maneuverability and shape adaptability in constrained underwater environments, but presents challenges in mechanical integration, dynamic modeling, and hydrodynamic characterization.
AI.method: Developed FoDeGlider with two independently actuated wings for large-range folding and deflection; created a multibody dynamics model treating wing configuration as a structural variable; formulated a composite rigid body algorithm (CRBA)-based projection to unify composite inertia, wrench transformations, and component-level hydrodynamics into a Fossen-form dynamic model; proposed a sequential parameter-identification framework to estimate fuselage and wing hydrodynamic coefficients, creating an open benchmark dataset.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrated accurate dynamic modeling and parameter identification across diverse morphing configurations; gate traversal experiments validated FoDeGlider's ability to actively reconfigure its morphology during locomotion, enabling enhanced navigation in confined underwater environments.
AI.conclusion: FoDeGlider successfully achieves enhanced navigation capabilities in confined underwater environments through its active morphing capabilities, demonstrating that configuration-dependent variations in mass distribution, center-of-geometry location, and hydrodynamic loading can be accurately captured and modeled.

title: From Language to Navigation Goals: A Vision-Language Approach for Semantic Navigation of Mobile Robots Using RGB-D Perception
summary:
Natural language interaction provides an intuitive way for non-expert users to communicate with robotic platforms. However, transforming user requests into executable navigation actions remains a challenging task, requiring the integration of language understanding, environment perception, and autonomous navigation. This work presents a language-driven navigation framework that enables mobile robots to interpret user requests in natural language to move the robot to a destination and autonomously navigate towards it.
  The framework is composed of modular ROS 2 components that cooperate to transform natural language instructions into navigation actions. Given a natural language request referring to a target in the environment (e.g., "go to the mail box"), the system identifies the referenced object, estimates its position using RGB-D data, and generates a navigation goal, which is then executed through the ROS 2 Nav2 navigation stack. The ROS 2-based implementation facilitates portability across different robotic platforms, requiring only the configuration of the corresponding topics and services.
  The system is evaluated in both simulation and real-world scenarios using a TurtleBot3 Waffle and a Unitree Go2 robot with a RealSense camera. Experimental results show that the framework successfully interprets both direct commands and contextual requests, generates meaningful natural-language feedback, and navigates towards the desired target. These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining semantic perception and autonomous navigation to provide an intuitive human-robot interaction paradigm. Code will be released as open source upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: A modular ROS 2 framework that enables mobile robots to interpret natural language requests and autonomously navigate to referenced targets using RGB-D perception.
AI.motivation: Natural language interaction is intuitive for non-experts, but transforming user requests into executable navigation actions remains challenging as it requires integrating language understanding, environment perception, and autonomous navigation.
AI.method: A language-driven navigation framework composed of modular ROS 2 components that: (1) identifies referenced objects from natural language requests, (2) estimates object positions using RGB-D data, (3) generates navigation goals, and (4) executes navigation through the ROS 2 Nav2 stack. The implementation is platform-agnostic, requiring only topic and service configuration.
AI.result: Evaluated on TurtleBot3 Waffle and Unitree Go2 robots with RealSense cameras in both simulation and real-world scenarios. The system successfully interprets direct commands and contextual requests, generates meaningful natural-language feedback, and navigates to desired targets.
AI.conclusion: The framework demonstrates the feasibility of combining semantic perception and autonomous navigation to provide an intuitive human-robot interaction paradigm, with code to be released as open source upon acceptance.

title: Design and Control of the "QuadBoat": A Quadruped Surface Vehicle for Drowning Rescue
summary: Prompt extraction of victims from water is crucial in water surface rescue missions. However, previous research on rescue robots has seldom addressed this issue. This paper presents QuadBoat, a bio-inspired unmanned surface vehicle (USV) designed to track and retrieve victims from water. QuadBoat features a quadrupedal robot configuration, enabling it with highly adaptable and agile maneuverability through its actively adjustable posture. Employing an inverse kinematics-based controller and cascaded model predictive control (MPC)-PID controller for overall movement, QuadBoat can accurately track and retrieve objects on the water surface. Maneuverability demonstrations validate QuadBoat's high agility, while a series of tracking experiments, including leg action tracking and trajectory tracking, confirm its high motion accuracy and system mobility. Finally, visual-based tracking and object pickup experiments further verify QuadBoat's target tracking capabilities and its effectiveness in executing rescues, both indoors and outdoors.

AI.tldr: QuadBoat is a bio-inspired USV with quadrupedal configuration that uses inverse kinematics and MPC-PID controllers to track and retrieve victims from water, demonstrating high agility, accuracy, and mobility in rescue missions.
AI.motivation: Victim extraction from water is critical in rescue missions, but previous research on rescue robots has rarely addressed this issue.
AI.method: QuadBoat features a quadrupedal robot configuration with actively adjustable posture. It employs an inverse kinematics-based controller and cascaded model predictive control (MPC)-PID controller for movement.
AI.result: Maneuverability demonstrations confirm high agility; tracking experiments (leg action and trajectory) verify high motion accuracy and system mobility; visual-based tracking and object pickup experiments validate target tracking capabilities and rescue effectiveness in indoor and outdoor environments.
AI.conclusion: QuadBoat is an effective rescue robot capable of accurately tracking and retrieving victims from water, demonstrating superior agility, precision, and mobility for water surface rescue missions.

title: Anatomy of Uncertainty: Expressive Descriptors of Robotic Manipulator Motion for Non-verbal Communication in Human-Robot Collaboration
summary: Robots operating in human-robot collaboration must communicate not only their intended actions but also uncertainty arising from incomplete or ambiguous perception. This work introduces a mathematical framework for expressing perceptual uncertainty through robotic manipulator motion. Drawing on Laban Movement Analysis, robot behavior is organized in a Commitment-Vigilance state space that maps uncertainty-related states - confidence, curiosity, hesitance, fear, and inactivity - to distinct Laban Effort signatures. Five motion primitives - approach, pause, retreat, exploration, and oscillation - are then parameterized using eleven kinematic and geometric descriptors, including acceleration, pause and retreat characteristics, gaze angles, tilt, and shiver amplitude. A video-based human-subject study evaluated recognition of four expressive trajectories and the influence of individual descriptors on perceived intensity. Participants reliably identified the intended behavioral states, while several descriptors significantly modulated expressiveness. The results establish a perceptually grounded basis for encoding robot uncertainty in motion and support future autonomous trajectory generation using parametric movement representations for collaborative tasks in shared environments. Code, videos, questionnaire and appendices are available at "https://bit.ly/github-aou".

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a mathematical framework for encoding perceptual uncertainty in robot motion through Laban Movement Analysis, with five motion primitives parameterized by eleven kinematic descriptors and validated via human-subject studies showing reliable recognition of behavioral states.
AI.motivation: Robots in human-robot collaboration must communicate not only intended actions but also uncertainty from incomplete perception; there is a need for a perceptually grounded basis for encoding uncertainty in motion.
AI.method: A Commitment-Vigilance state space maps uncertainty states (confidence, curiosity, hesitance, fear, inactivity) to Laban Effort signatures; five motion primitives (approach, pause, retreat, exploration, oscillation) are parameterized using eleven kinematic/geometric descriptors; a video-based human-subject study evaluated recognition of four expressive trajectories and descriptor influence on perceived intensity.
AI.result: Participants reliably identified intended behavioral states, and several descriptors significantly modulated expressiveness, establishing that the framework effectively encodes perceptual uncertainty in motion that humans can understand.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a perceptually grounded basis for encoding robot uncertainty in motion, supporting future autonomous trajectory generation using parametric movement representations for collaborative tasks in shared environments.

title: Towards a Modular Bin-picking Framework for Handling Object Pose Uncertainties
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, keywords: bin picking; object manipulation; grasping strategies; object pose distribution estimation
summary:
In recent years, there has been growing interest in robust robotic systems for precise bin-picking applications. To achieve reliable performance, such systems must address errors arising from both the object pose estimation and the grasping process. Although various approaches have been proposed, they typically target specific challenges and do not offer general solutions. In this paper, we present a modular framework that jointly handles both error types. The framework incorporates object pose distribution estimation to account for pose uncertainty, which frequently arises in situations with ambiguous observations where a single correct pose cannot be determined. To further reduce uncertainty, we introduce a second-viewpoint module that computes complementary pose distributions, which are subsequently fused. This fusion decreases overall uncertainty and improves system efficiency. Additionally, two independent modules are included to compensate for grasping errors. The modular design allows the components to be combined for optimal performance or used individually, depending on the physical setup.
  The proposed method is evaluated in a real-world setup with three different objects, with no errors, and all modules are shown to improve efficiency. These results suggest that incorporating pose distributions with grasping pose errors is a promising direction for developing more flexible and reliable robotic production systems.
  To the best of our knowledge, this is the first framework that jointly addresses both grasping and object pose uncertainties using interchangeable modules. We believe there is ample opportunity to integrate additional modules, resulting in improved performance and flexibility. The current framework is limited to pose uncertainties in SO(2), but it could be extended to SE(3), enabling additional modules to improve the system.

AI.tldr: A modular framework for robust robotic bin-picking that jointly handles object pose uncertainty and grasping errors through interchangeable components.
AI.motivation: Robotic bin-picking systems must address errors from both object pose estimation and grasping process. Existing approaches typically target specific challenges without providing general solutions.
AI.method: Incorporates object pose distribution estimation for pose uncertainty, a second-viewpoint module that computes complementary pose distributions which are fused, and two independent modules to compensate for grasping errors. The modular design allows components to be combined for optimal performance or used individually.
AI.result: Evaluated with three objects in a real-world setup with no errors; all modules improve efficiency. The approach demonstrates that incorporating pose distributions with grasping pose errors is a promising direction for developing flexible and reliable robotic production systems.
AI.conclusion: First framework to jointly address both grasping and object pose uncertainties using interchangeable modules. Can be extended from SO(2) to SE(3), enabling additional modules to improve system performance and flexibility.

title: nuTruck: Benchmarking Autonomous Driving Planning for Distributed Electric-drive Trucks
summary: The dominance of traditional rule-based methods in autonomous driving has gradually been replaced by learning-based approaches. While learning-based planners have achieved considerable success in passenger vehicles, their performance on heavy-duty trucks, particularly modern distributed electric-drive trucks (DETs), remains largely unexplored. To facilitate research and application of learning-based planners in DETs, this letter presents the first high-fidelity benchmark, called nuTruck, designed to support large-scale neural network training and closed-loop evaluation. Given the complex dynamics and high rollover susceptibility of DETs, we first incorporate a highly accurate nonlinear truck dynamical model into the simulation, which enables independent driving and steering of all wheels and captures dynamic load transfer caused by acceleration, deceleration, and cornering, thereby allowing quantitative assessment of rollover risk in closed-loop simulation. Second, we adapt several rule-based and learning-based planners as baselines for DETs and evaluate their performance in closed-loop simulation. Finally, using real-world driving scenarios from the nuPlan dataset, we conduct extensive closed-loop evaluations, analyzing not only conventional collision-free planning performance, but also the dynamical safety of the planned trajectories. The proposed nuTruck benchmark is expected to serve as a new standard for fair and realistic evaluation of autonomous driving planners on DETs.

AI.tldr: A high-fidelity benchmark called nuTruck for evaluating learning-based autonomous driving planners on modern distributed electric-drive trucks (DETs), incorporating accurate nonlinear dynamics and rollover risk assessment.
AI.motivation: Learning-based planners succeed for passenger vehicles but performance on heavy-duty trucks, especially modern distributed electric-drive trucks (DETs), remains unexplored, requiring a specialized benchmark.
AI.method: 1) Incorporates highly accurate nonlinear truck dynamical model with independent wheel steering/driving and dynamic load transfer capture; 2) Adapts rule-based and learning-based planners as baselines; 3) Uses real-world nuPlan dataset scenarios for closed-loop evaluation.
AI.result: nuTruck enables quantitative assessment of rollover risk and comprehensive evaluation of both collision-free planning performance and dynamical safety on DETs.
AI.conclusion: nuTruck serves as a new standard for fair and realistic evaluation of autonomous driving planners specifically designed for heavy-duty trucks.

title: The Nonsmooth Impact Direction (NSID) of Robotic Systems
summary: Collisions of rigid-link robots and rigid environments are often modeled as instantaneous events. Under this idealization, the impact forces become impulsive and the system velocities nonsmooth. In this work, we systematically analyze pre- and post-impact velocities focusing on what we refer to as the nonsmooth impact direction (NSID). We show that it is a characteristic direction of a robotic impact and largely independent of contact properties. The results are directly applicable to large classes of backdrivable robotic systems with rigid links. We address particularities of systems with nonelastic and flexible joints, unconstrained as well as constrained systems. Further, we show that the approach direction w.r.t the NSID sets the direction of the impulsive force in frictional, inelastic impacts. The comprehensive theoretical analysis of this work supported by an experimental validation may serve as a foundation for future planning and control algorithms for various robotic impact applications. These can include humanoid locomotion on a slippery surface or repetitive hammering.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically analyzes pre- and post-impact velocities in robotic collisions, identifying a characteristic nonsmooth impact direction (NSID) that largely determines the impulsive force direction and is independent of contact properties.
AI.motivation: Collisions of rigid-link robots with rigid environments are modeled as instantaneous events where impact forces become impulsive and system velocities are nonsmooth. A comprehensive theoretical framework is needed to understand and control these impact behaviors.
AI.method: The authors perform a comprehensive theoretical analysis of robotic impacts focusing on the nonsmooth impact direction (NSID), examining its properties and characteristics. They address various system configurations including systems with nonelastic/flexible joints, unconstrained and constrained systems, and frictional impacts. Experimental validation is provided to support the theoretical findings.
AI.result: They demonstrate that the NSID is a characteristic direction of robotic impact largely independent of contact properties, and that the approach direction relative to the NSID determines the direction of the impulsive force in frictional, inelastic impacts.
AI.conclusion: This theoretical framework provides a foundation for future planning and control algorithms in robotic impact applications such as humanoid locomotion on slippery surfaces and repetitive hammering.

title: Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem for Multi-Rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
comment: 28 pages, 10 figures, preprint submitted to European Journal of Operational Research
summary: This paper introduces the Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem (DVOP), a generalization of the Orienteering Problem (OP). The OP maximizes the reward collected from spatial targets under a limited travel budget; the DVOP extends it by accounting for both external and vehicle-actuated forces. We study the DVOP in the context of multi-rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flight planning, using a three-dimensional Point-Mass Model (PMM) constrained by maximum velocity and acceleration magnitudes and subject to gravitational acceleration, with the travel budget expressed as a maximum flight time. Because the DVOP couples reward maximization with time-optimal trajectory planning, it cannot be formulated as a simple graph problem and solved exactly without relaxing or under-actuating the vehicle dynamics. We therefore propose two solution approaches: a Branch-and-Bound (BnB) procedure that combines Non-Linear Programming (NLP) and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to provide high-quality solutions, and a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) metaheuristic that supplies an initial reward bound and scales to instances intractable for the BnB. The BnB relies on a novel MILP formulation of travel costs based on minimum-time trajectory primitives through target triplets, yielding a tight reward upper bound, while the LNS uses limited thrust decomposition to compute fast, high-quality PMM trajectories. Experiments on benchmark instances show improvements of up to 37 % over state-of-the-art solutions for the Kinematic Orienteering Problem, and a real-world deployment on a multi-rotor UAV verifies the proposed PMM solution trajectories.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem (DVOP), a generalization of the Orienteering Problem that couples reward maximization with time-optimal trajectory planning for multi-rotor UAVs using a 3D Point-Mass Model. It proposes a Branch-and-Bound (BnB) combining NLP and MILP for high-quality solutions, and a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) metaheuristic for scaling to intractable instances, achieving up to 37% improvement over state-of-the-art solutions.
AI.motivation: The traditional Orienteering Problem (OP) maximizes rewards from spatial targets under a travel budget, but it doesn't account for vehicle dynamics. The authors extend OP to the Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem (DVOP) to properly model multi-rotor UAV flight planning where reward maximization must be coupled with time-optimal trajectory planning under realistic physical constraints (velocity, acceleration, gravity).
AI.method: Two solution approaches are proposed: (1) Branch-and-Bound (BnB) combining Non-Linear Programming (NLP) and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), using a novel MILP formulation of travel costs based on minimum-time trajectory primitives through target triplets; (2) Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) metaheuristic using limited thrust decomposition for fast, high-quality PMM trajectories. The 3D Point-Mass Model (PMM) with maximum velocity/acceleration constraints and gravity is used for trajectory computation.
AI.result: Experiments on benchmark instances show up to 37% improvement over state-of-the-art solutions for the Kinematic Orienteering Problem. A real-world deployment on a multi-rotor UAV verified the proposed PMM solution trajectories, demonstrating the practical applicability of the approach.
AI.conclusion: The DVOP effectively models the coupling between reward maximization and time-optimal trajectory planning for UAVs. The BnB method provides high-quality solutions while LNS scales to intractable instances, with both approaches validated through extensive benchmark testing and real-world UAV deployment, achieving significant improvements over existing methods.

title: Vision-Based Obstacle Separation for Strawberry Harvesting in Clusters Using Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
summary: Selective harvesting in clustered strawberry environments is challenging because ripe fruits are often occluded by surrounding unripe fruits, making direct grasping unreliable. To address this problem, this paper proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, termed VGPA, which integrates a vision-guided decision mechanism and a Progressive Adaptive Exploration Strategy (PAES) for vision-based obstacle separation and harvesting. The task was decomposed into two sequential stages: obstacle separation and target grasping. At the high level, the vision-guided mechanism improved option selection and accelerated policy convergence. At the low level, PAES improved exploration efficiency and training stability during continuous control learning. In simulation experiments, the learned policy achieved a success rate of 96.7%. In addition, sim-to-real transfer experiments on a self-developed parallel robot showed that the proposed method achieved success rates ranging from 71.7% to 88.3%, outperforming direct picking while requiring only 1.22~s more average harvesting time. These results verified the effectiveness, generalization ability, and practical potential of the proposed method for robotic harvesting in complex clustered environments.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical reinforcement learning framework (VGPA) combining vision-guided decision-making and Progressive Adaptive Exploration Strategy (PAES) for robotic strawberry harvesting in clustered environments.
AI.motivation: Selective harvesting in clustered strawberry environments is challenging because ripe fruits are often occluded by surrounding unripe fruits, making direct grasping unreliable.
AI.method: The paper proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework (VGPA) that integrates a vision-guided decision mechanism and a Progressive Adaptive Exploration Strategy (PAES), decomposing the task into two sequential stages: obstacle separation and target grasping.
AI.result: The learned policy achieved 96.7% success rate in simulation. In sim-to-real transfer experiments on a self-developed parallel robot, the method achieved success rates ranging from 71.7% to 88.3%, outperforming direct picking while requiring only 1.22~s more average harvesting time.
AI.conclusion: The results verified the effectiveness, generalization ability, and practical potential of the proposed method for robotic harvesting in complex clustered environments.

title: Learning Robust Execution in Robotic Manipulation with Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Robotic manipulation poses fundamental challenges due to uncertainty, long-horizon execution, and compounding errors, which can easily destabilize execution and lead to task failure. Although recent vision-language-action (VLA) models exhibit strong generalization, they typically lack explicit mechanisms to assess execution stability and to recover when execution deviates from its nominal behavior. In this paper, we propose: (1) two complementary metrics to assess execution quality at runtime, and (2) an agentic reinforcement learning framework that learns to restore effective execution through high-level decision-making rather than directly learning low-level actions. In this framework, an agentic policy reasons over recent execution history and selects among a small set of execution modes to regulate the execution process. Under execution degradation, it triggers appropriate recovery mechanisms to restore the robot to previously visited nominal states, enabling the task to continue. We evaluate the proposed method on the LIBERO benchmark, achieving up to a 13.7% improvement in success rate under standard settings and up to a 39.2% improvement under disturbance settings, demonstrating substantially enhanced execution robustness.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces two runtime quality metrics and an agentic reinforcement learning framework that uses high-level decision-making to restore effective robotic execution when deviations occur, achieving significant success rate improvements on the LIBERO benchmark.
AI.motivation: Robotic manipulation faces fundamental challenges from uncertainty, long-horizon execution, and compounding errors that can destabilize execution and cause task failure. While recent vision-language-action (VLA) models show strong generalization, they lack explicit mechanisms to assess execution stability and recover when execution deviates from nominal behavior.
AI.method: The method consists of: (1) two complementary metrics to assess execution quality at runtime, and (2) an agentic reinforcement learning framework that learns to restore effective execution through high-level decision-making rather than directly learning low-level actions. The agentic policy reasons over recent execution history and selects among a small set of execution modes to regulate the process, triggering appropriate recovery mechanisms to restore the robot to previously visited nominal states when execution degrades.
AI.result: Evaluated on the LIBERO benchmark, the method achieves up to a 13.7% improvement in success rate under standard settings and up to a 39.2% improvement under disturbance settings, demonstrating substantially enhanced execution robustness.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach successfully addresses the fundamental challenges of robotic manipulation by providing runtime execution quality assessment and recovery mechanisms through high-level decision-making, significantly improving task success rates compared to approaches lacking these capabilities.

title: Recursive ArUco Markers: A Scalable Fiducial Marker Design for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Landing Pads
summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) increasingly rely on visual fiducial markers for autonomous navigation and precision landing. However, standard markers suffer from limited operational ranges, becoming undetectable when the camera is either too far or too close. While recursive and fractal markers have been proposed to address this issue, existing approaches either require the marker's center to remain visible, making them vulnerable to occlusion, or are limited in their recursion depth and placement. We propose a novel Recursive ArUco marker design. Our method allows any standard fiducial marker to be transformed into a recursive marker with an arbitrary depth. By employing a modified bit-sampling strategy during detection, we embed complete markers within both the black and white bits of the parent marker. This approach guarantees unlimited recursion depth and robust detection even with partial occlusion, as it does not rely on the marker's center being visible. Furthermore, by maintaining a single, unique identifier across all recursive scales, our proposal provides an extensive dictionary of multiple unique landing pads. This capability allows fleets of UAVs to operate simultaneously, with each drone landing at its designated location -- a feature not supported by existing Fractal and Harco markers due to their structural and dictionary constraints.

AI.tldr: A novel Recursive ArUco marker design transforms any standard marker into a recursive marker with arbitrary depth, embedding complete markers within both black and white bits of the parent marker. This enables unlimited recursion depth, robust detection even with partial occlusion, and multiple unique landing pads for simultaneous UAV operations.
AI.motivation: Standard fiducial markers have limited operational ranges and are undetectable when cameras are too far or too close. Existing recursive and fractal markers either require the marker's center to be visible (vulnerable to occlusion), have limited recursion depth/placement, or cannot support multiple unique landing pads simultaneously.
AI.method: The proposed method transforms any standard ArUco marker into a recursive marker with arbitrary depth using a modified bit-sampling strategy during detection. Complete markers are embedded within both black and white bits of the parent marker, maintaining a single unique identifier across all recursive scales to create an extensive dictionary of multiple unique landing pads.
AI.result: The approach guarantees unlimited recursion depth and robust detection even with partial occlusion, as it does not rely on the marker's center being visible. It supports multiple unique landing pads that can be used simultaneously by different UAVs, enabling fleets to operate with each drone landing at its designated location.
AI.conclusion: Unlike existing Fractal and Harco markers that lack simultaneous landing pad capability due to structural and dictionary constraints, this Recursive ArUco marker design enables coordinated multi-UAV operations where each drone can autonomously land at its specific designated location.

title: Merging Reaction to Cognition: A Hybrid Cognitive Strategy for Odour Source Localisation in Natural Environments
summary: Chemical pollutants released into the environment are transported by turbulent flows, generating complex, intermittent plume structures that threaten ecosystems and human health. Rapid localisation of emission sources is critical, and field robots equipped with chemical sensors provide a viable means to perform this task.
